is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses exclusively on Aedes aegypti, as stated in the title and abstract (Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study identifies selective sweeps in Aedes aegypti and does not report genotypes for the specific Anopheles resistance markers listed in the criteria (Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports sweep classifications for genomic windows but does not provide specific genotype or allele counts for resistance markers (Page 5, Table 1).

african_field_population.evidence: The study includes population samples from Gabon (Franceville), Senegal (Ngoye), and Kenya (Kaya Bomu) (Page 3, Figure 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article analyzing genomic data for selective sweeps (Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific collection sites such as Franceville, Ngoye, and Kaya Bomu are identified (Page 3, Figure 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection years for the mosquito samples are not explicitly provided in the text (Page 10).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study re-analyses a dataset of 104 individuals previously described in Love et al. (2023) and Rose et al. (2020) (Page 10).

supplement.evidence: The paper refers to supplementary tables (e.g., Table S3, S4) for the complete list of sweep calls and candidate genes (Page 10).

assessment.summary: This study applies a machine learning approach (diploS/HIC) to whole-genome sequencing data from Aedes aegypti populations in Africa (Gabon, Senegal, Kenya) and the Americas (Brazil) to identify selective sweeps. The authors find that soft selective sweeps are the predominant mode of adaptation and identify several candidate insecticide resistance genes, such as cytochrome P450s and GSTs, within these sweep regions.
